findings.message: cmd_size counts lines in two different ways that disagree. Tracked files go through `git diff --numstat`, which reports binaries as `-` and leaves them out. Untracked files go through `xargs -0 cat | wc -l`, which counts the newline bytes inside binaries. It also misses the last line of a text file with no trailing newline. As a result, the same file gets a different count depending only on whether it has been `git add`ed. Fix: count untracked files with numstat as well. Either run `git diff --no-index --numstat /dev/null <file>` per file, or stage them intent-to-add in a temporary index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE` copy plus `git add -N`) and use a single `git diff --numstat`. Add a test row for an untracked binary and for a file with no trailing newline.
findings.scenario: pr.size_cap 10, an untracked `src/logo.png` containing 12 0x0a bytes, plus 3 tracked production lines → reported as 15 lines, exit 1 (FAIL). After `git add src/logo.png` the same tree reports 3 lines, exit 0.

findings.message: Every internal failure of the done guard is reported as 'nothing missing'. `missing 2>/dev/null` drops stderr, and `|| exit 0` exits 0 with no output, so the user is never told the guard did not run. Examples are `git diff` against the merge-base failing under `set -e`/`pipefail`, or `ls .specclaw/changes` failing. Not blocking is a valid choice, but a silent exit is not. Exit 1 with a one-line 'specclaw: done guard did not run: <last error>' on stderr instead. Claude Code shows that as a non-blocking hook error and does not trap the turn. Add a test that drives a real git failure and expects the notice.
findings.scenario: Corrupt `.git/index` in a repo where change 002-x has every task done and no verify → `git diff --name-only $mb` fails → done-guard exits 0 with empty stderr, which is the same result as a fully verified change. The turn stops with no indication that the check never ran.

findings.message: The size verdict depends on the merge-base commit it was compared against. The skill tells verify to record this line in the verify report, but the success, over-cap and waiver lines never name the base ref or the merge-base SHA. Only the git-failure line prints `${mb:0:10}`. Add `against <base> @ ${mb:0:10}` to every line that reports a count.
findings.scenario: Verify records 'size cap: 380 production lines (cap 400)'. Main is then merged into the change branch and the merge-base moves, so a re-run reports 120. The persisted report gives no way to tell which merge-base the 380 was measured against.

findings.message: The waiver regex accepts bullets and bold, but not other common Markdown spellings. A heading (`## Size waiver` with the reason on the next line or after the colon) is not matched, nor is underscore emphasis (`_Size waiver:_ reason` / `__Size waiver__: reason`). Either widen the pattern to cover `#+` prefixes and `_` emphasis, or document the exact accepted form in verify.md and the config template.
